title: Query Basics
description: Define and execute queries in GraphQL.

data.text: Queries are how clients read data from your GraphQL API. In Hot Chocolate, any method on a class registered with `AddQueryType` becomes a query field.
Create a `Query` class and decorate methods with `[Query]`. The method name becomes the field name unless you override it.

data.title: Query Class
data.content: Expose a list of books and a single book lookup.

data.text: Query methods can accept arguments. The parameter name becomes the argument name in the schema.

data.title: Query with Arguments
Dependency Injection
data.text: Hot Chocolate resolves constructor dependencies from the ASP.NET Core DI container. Inject repositories instead of using static data.
Always use async methods when querying a database. Hot Chocolate supports `Task<T>` and `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` return types.

data.title: Async Query
data.content: Return Task for async database calls.

terms.definition: An entry point on the Query type that clients can call.
A value passed to a query field to filter or modify the result.
A query method that returns Task<T> for non-blocking I/O.

data.title: Build a Search Query
data.description: Create a search query that accepts a string and returns matching books by title or author (case-insensitive).
steps: Create a Search method with a string query parameter
Filter where Title or Author contains the query
data.expectedOutcome: Running search(query: "graphql") returns only books with "graphql" in the title or author name.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Methods on Query classes become query fields
Parameters become arguments in the schema
Always use async for database access
